solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: "Must" could clue it!

indicators.note: the clue says the quoted word could become the entry, signalling its letters may be rearranged to produce it

blocks.note: the quoted word taken as written, which is also its definition

explanation.surface: A setter muses that a single word would make a neat clue all by itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted word is both the fodder and the definition: rearranged it gives STUM, which means must (new wine).
explanation.definitionFit: Stum is grape juice before fermentation, which is the winemaking sense of must.

clue.text: Arranges a hoist in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so what follows is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a raise is a lift or hoist

explanation.surface: Someone sets up lifting gear inside a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To array troops or items is to set them out in order, a synonym of arranges.

clue.text: Fruit from old city fed to divine being

indicators.note: food fed to a creature goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a deity
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An offering of fruit from an ancient city is presented to a god.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is the hard-skinned fruit of plants in the squash family.

clue.text: Rebel fighter, not the first old person likely to go wrong

definitions.text: old person likely to go wrong

indicators.note: not the first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word clued

blocks.note: an insurgent using violence

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter is described as an old hand who is apt to slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the T of TERRORIST leaves ERRORIST, an obsolete Chambers word for one who errs; 'old' flags it as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: An errorist, in the old sense, is someone who errs or holds mistaken views.

clue.text: Got waxy in mathematical function in bar

indicators.note: in places the trigonometric piece inside the other one

blocks.note: a rod is a bar
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Someone got angry over a maths function in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxy' is British slang for cross, but here it means coated with resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosined means rubbed with rosin, the solid resin violinists put on bows, so made waxy or sticky.

clue.text: Sadly lacking essence, the cool cat

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly, so the letters are disordered
the essence of a word is its central letter, and lacking it means taking that out

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter is lost
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cool cat is mocked for having no real substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The essence of 'the' is its middle letter H; remove it and rearrange the rest with COOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Instrument of torture and destruction

blocks.note: first meaning: a frame on which victims were stretched
second meaning: ruin, as in the phrase 'go to ... and ruin'

explanation.surface: A dungeon device is described as a means of torment and ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the stretching frame, and in the idiom with ruin it is a variant of wrack, meaning wreckage.

clue.text: Verse with urgent message little person brought in

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the distress signal
tich (or titch) is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A poem arrives as an urgent message carried in by a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A stichos is a single line of verse, especially in Greek poetry.

clue.text: One of the bivalve molluscs to count and measure

blocks.note: to tell is to count, as in telling votes
an en is a printer's measure

explanation.surface: A shellfish is set to be counted and measured, like a survey sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellen is a Chambers variant of tellin, a thin-shelled bivalve shellfish.

clue.text: Plant seen in vegetable baskets on poles

indicators.note: something seen in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a salad vegetable
to set seeds is to plant them

explanation.surface: A plant is found among vegetable baskets hung on poles at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun but is the verb SET, placed within the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket of burning fuel mounted on a pole as a beacon or torch.

clue.text: Protest or act in unruly manner — waves being used to convey message

definitions.text: waves being used to convey message

indicators.note: acting unruly means behaving out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Demonstrators behave rowdily, sending out their message on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Troposcatter is radio communication by bouncing waves off irregularities in the lower atmosphere.

clue.text: Bull, thankless animal

indicators.note: thankless means without thanks, so the short word for thanks is removed

blocks.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A bull is called an ungrateful beast.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks; taking it from TAURUS leaves the answer. 'Bull' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The urus is the aurochs, the extinct wild ox of Europe.

clue.text: Dry bit of roof that can be cut without damage

definitions.text: that can be cut without damage

blocks.note: sec is the wine term for dry
a roof is covered in tiles

explanation.surface: A dry roof tile can be trimmed without breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectile describes a mineral that can be sliced cleanly with a knife without shattering.

clue.text: Cast rarely given a celebratory message — heartless!

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: a toast is a celebratory speech or salute

explanation.surface: A rarely seen actor's cast gets a cold, heartless toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' marks the answer as an archaic form: tost is an old past tense of toss.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossed means thrown, a synonym of cast, and tost is its rare old spelling.

clue.text: Latin poet a ceremonial officer listened to

indicators.note: listened to means we go by how the word sounds rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a marshal organises ceremonies

explanation.surface: A Roman poet is heeded by a court official.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial was the first-century Roman writer of satirical epigrams.

clue.text: Fuel providing elevated level of force, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: high is elevated, and a dyne is a unit of force

explanation.surface: A fuel is praised for delivering a lot of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydyne is a liquid rocket propellant used in early US launch vehicles.

clue.text: Criminal is shifty, showing display of petulance

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shifty-looking crook throws a sulky tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissy fit is an informal term for a tantrum or bout of petulant temper.

clue.text: A fictional work's being seen as dead?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the remains of the dead

blocks.note: taken as written
She is H. Rider Haggard's novel, plus 's for 'is'

explanation.surface: A novel is accused of being lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: In Haggard's She the immortal Ayesha crumbles to dust, which makes the question mark apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the cremated remains of a person, so they stand in for the dead.

clue.text: Victorian scientist revealing crop's quality

blocks.note: wheat is a cereal crop, plus 's
tone is quality of sound or character

explanation.surface: A Victorian scientist studies the quality of a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Wheatstone was a Victorian physicist, inventor of the concertina and the Wheatstone bridge.

clue.text: Requirement after horse race entry is announced

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a way in is an entrance

explanation.surface: After the race, a horse's entry for the next is declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys must be weighed after a race to confirm they carried the correct weight; that check is the weigh-in.

clue.text: Look for decisive victory, do, when faced with judge

blocks.note: to see is to judge or consider
a knockout
ut is the old name for the note do (doh) in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A boxer chases a knockout, then has to appear before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When faced with judge' puts the judge piece in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek out is to search for something deliberately, a phrasal synonym of look for.

clue.text: Needs spies to be deployed in haste

indicators.note: deploying troops spreads them into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intelligence chief needs agents sent out urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Speediness is the quality of being quick, a synonym of haste.

clue.text: Criticise Byron's daughter for being a saucy dish

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it
Ada Lovelace was Lord Byron's daughter

explanation.surface: Someone attacks Ada Lovelace for being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheeky, but it literally means made with sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Panada is a thick paste or sauce of breadcrumbs, used as a base or served as a pap.

clue.text: English girl is equal to Bard

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
informal for girl

explanation.surface: An English girl is the equal of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To Bard' means as Shakespeare used it: egal is his word for equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Egal is an archaic Shakespearean form of equal, from French égal.

clue.text: Pub makes money, it's said, and puts in storage jars

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is judged by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, and to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: A pub turns a profit and stockpiles goods in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place something, especially ashes, in an urn, a kind of jar.

clue.text: Hint chap's given in game

blocks.note: a tip is a hint
cat is old slang for a chap, plus 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A man receives a tip during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a traditional game in which a tapered stick is struck at one end to flip it up and then hit.

clue.text: Antelope in India featured in long tale

indicators.note: a thing featured in a story appears inside it

blocks.note: a saga is a lengthy story
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An antelope from India appears in a long story.
explanation.definitionFit: The saiga is a Central Asian antelope with a distinctive bulbous nose.

clue.text: Fish sale on island

blocks.note: vend as a noun means a sale
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Fish are being sold on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Vendis is a variant of vendace, a small whitefish found in a few British lakes.

clue.text: Maiden in state of ignorance gets money no more

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to be in the dark is to be ignorant
M is maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A naive young woman comes into money that no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency until the euro replaced it, so it is money that is gone.

clue.text: Local population is crazy, not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half the word survives, the rest being cut off

blocks.note: demented means crazy

explanation.surface: The locals are said to be completely mad, in a British 'not half' way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which disguises the instruction to keep half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deme is a township in ancient Attica, or in biology a local interbreeding population.

clue.text: Dishevelled male, not restricted going about

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: unkept means not held or retained
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A scruffy man roams about freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt means untidy or messy in appearance, a synonym of dishevelled.

clue.text: Sound of bell in bar

blocks.note: first meaning: the slow ringing of a bell
second meaning: in law, to bar or defeat a claim

explanation.surface: A bell is heard ringing in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; here it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolls when rung slowly; in Scots and English law to toll an action is to bar it.

clue.text: Dad spending time to cross lake to get unknown mineral

indicators.note: spending something uses it up so it is gone, so a letter leaves the word
to cross here means to span across, so one part is put around another

blocks.note: a father
standard abbreviation, the letter that goes
standard abbreviation
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A father takes time to travel across a lake to fetch an unfamiliar mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: FATHER loses its T to give FAHER, which goes round L, then Z is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Fahlerz is the German name for tetrahedrite, a grey copper ore mineral.

clue.text: Food giving bad taste, mostly egg

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: Chambers gives tack as a disagreeable taste
an egg is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A dish leaves a nasty taste, being mostly egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: One manual editor dismally lacking a simple form of language

indicators.note: dismally suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled
lacking means without, so a letter is removed from the mix

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written
the letter taken away

explanation.surface: A single handbook editor is poorly lacking a plain style of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom Neutral was an artificial international language devised around 1902 with a simplified grammar.

clue.text: Rock in ground left abandoned — last bit in the specified area

indicators.note: abandoning the abbreviation for left means dropping that letter from the word
last bit in points at the final letter of the next word only

blocks.note: land is ground
the final letter of the word
a site is a designated area

explanation.surface: A rock lies on abandoned ground, the last piece in a designated zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Andesite is a fine-grained volcanic rock named after the Andes.
